title: Love of Allah
hook: say, if you love Allah, follow me, and Allah will love you (3:31)

segments.voice: Yesterday, rida, contentment, and your line: pleased with him. Did the small thing you were arguing with get any quieter? Today, the station of love. Day one thousand two hundred seventy-eight.

"If ye love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins." That's the Qur'an, in Pickthall's translation, telling the Prophet ﷺ what to say. Read it slowly, because it's built in three moves. It starts with a condition: if you love. It turns on an action: follow me. And it ends with something coming back the other way: Allah will love you. Love isn't left as a feeling you announce. It's tested by what you do next. Today, love, as this verse frames it.
screen: `IF YE LOVE ALLAH.` → `FOLLOW ME.` → `ALLAH WILL LOVE YOU.`

segments.voice: The word is mahabbah, love. It is not only a word for poets. It is in the Qur'an, and it runs in both directions. In Pickthall's translation of another verse, Allah will bring "a people whom He loveth and who love Him." He loves first in that line. So how does a person grow in it? The verse we started with says: follow. Love shows up as imitation. People who love someone start to pick up their habits, their words, the way they treat others. Then there's a hadith qudsi, words the Prophet reported from Allah, in Sahih al-Bukhari, and it lays out the path step by step. My servant draws near to Me with nothing dearer to Me than what I have made obligatory. And My servant keeps drawing near with extra deeds until I love him. And when I love him, I become the hearing he hears with, the sight he sees with, the hand he holds with, the foot he walks with. Commentators are careful here. They warn against reading it as Allah becoming a person's body, and read it as a life so guided that the person hears, sees and acts as Allah would love. The order matters again: the duties, then the extra, then the love, then a whole life changed by it. Love here doesn't start as a feeling you chase. It follows the steps, and then it changes the one who walks them.
screen: `LOVE RUNS BOTH WAYS.` · `LOVE SHOWS UP AS FOLLOWING.` · `DUTIES, THEN EXTRA, THEN LOVE.` · `THE HEARING HE HEARS WITH.`

segments.voice: The practice: do one thing for love of Him. Settle, and breathe. Think of the extra deeds in the hadith, the ones nobody asks for. A short prayer beyond the required ones. A kind word to someone who can't return it. Picking up litter on a street that isn't yours. Feeding a bird. Choose one you could do today. Then ask yourself why you'd do it. Not for thanks, not to feel good about yourself. Just for love of the One you're doing it for. If you pray, you can hold the verse: if ye love Allah, follow me. If not, hold the plain thought: this is for love. The bell holds the time.
Mahabbah. Love: Allah's love for His servants and theirs for Him, shown by following and drawing near. Today's word.
Your line: love follows. Today, do the one extra thing you chose, quietly, and don't tell anyone. Tomorrow, fear and hope. Day one thousand two hundred seventy-eight.

howItsDone: Muslims speak of love of Allah as shown by following the Prophet's example and drawing near through required and voluntary worship, and teachers of the inward path describe it as one of the stations of the path.
